newsitem.title: USA: Armey predicts tough vote on China MFN status.
newsitem.headline: Armey predicts tough vote on China MFN status.

text.p: House Republican Leader Dick Armey on Tuesday predicted a tough fight later this year over renewing China's most favored nation trading status.
"If the vote were held today I couldn't tell you how it would go and I couldn't tell you how I would vote," Armey told reporters.
"This is going to be a tough thing. It's going to be a tough vote, it's one of those votes that brings you to a moment of truth," he said.
Armey said despite his commitment to free trade, he was struggling with the issue, adding that China needed to show tangible improvement on human rights and other issues.

President Clinton must decide by June whether to renew China's preferential trading status. His decision will then be debated by Congress. Administration officials have already said they expect Clinton to renew MFN to China.

Armey said he would not consider it any imminent danger to the U.S. economy if Congress did not vote to renew MFN. He also suggested it might be a healthy thing for Chinese officials to have to come to terms with a "no" vote.
